expectations.text: Flags the application-and-review enrollment as the core defect: eligible developers who miss the paperwork silently pay the full rate
expectations.evidence: "Manual application is the 'opt-in waiver' failure mode... a qualifying developer who misses the paperwork silently pays full rate."

expectations.text: Requires defaulting eligible developers into the waiver automatically rather than making them opt in
expectations.evidence: "Fix: default eligible vendors in."; "Enrollment: none."

expectations.text: States the reason: an opt-in waiver changes paper rather than behavior
expectations.evidence: The reason given is silent full-rate payment and delay, not 'changes paper rather than behavior'.

expectations.text: Challenges the $400,000 threshold against the roughly $1M revenue threshold that major marketplace waiver programs cluster around, and recommends anchoring there rather than inventing a number
expectations.evidence: "$400K sits below the $1M anchor... That's allowed, but it needs data." The rewrite keeps $400K and does not recommend the $1M anchor.

expectations.text: Names annual-reset versus lifetime cap as an explicit design decision to make rather than a detail
expectations.evidence: "Annual reset is the default. Lifetime (Shopify's 2025 change)... decide deliberately."

expectations.text: Notes that moving from an annual reset to a lifetime cap is a one-way tightening
expectations.evidence: "Lifetime (Shopify's 2025 change) is a one-way tightening"

expectations.text: Flags the per-entity allowance as a gap and requires associated or affiliated accounts to aggregate toward the cap
expectations.evidence: "Per-entity $400K allowance is a loophole"; "one allowance per vendor group."

expectations.text: Requires a stated rule for what happens when a vendor crosses the threshold mid-period
expectations.evidence: Draft "silent on mid-quarter crossings"; the rewrite uses a marginal 0%-on-first-$400K-then-15% shape.

expectations.text: Classifies the draft as a revenue-exemption tier and identifies that shape as the default waiver rung on efficiency grounds
expectations.evidence: "a revenue-exemption tier is the skill's default rung."

expectations.text: States that fee waivers are a standard menu item across major marketplaces rather than an exceptional discount
expectations.evidence: Cites Apple, Atlassian and Shopify precedents for specific mechanics but never says waivers are standard.

expectations.text: Names waiver coverage among eligible developers as the post-launch metric proving the default-in rule worked, and pairs the waiver with a published notice commitment for later changes
expectations.evidence: "Waiver coverage among eligible vendors. It should be about 100%"; "Six months' notice for unfavorable changes".
